title: The ordered left coefficient square for a specified compactification
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes and morphisms are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings and let $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilate both. On small ordinary etale sites use the constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $\mathcal C_{T,R}=D^b_{ctf}(T_{et},R)$ for the full subcategory of complexes with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, meaning that derived tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer]. Put $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$, and $R_T(d)=R_T(1)^{\otimes d}$ for $d\geq0$, with $R_T(0)=R_T$ [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line].
Let $S$ be a base, let $X_0=S$, $X_{r+1}=\mathbf A^1_{X_r}$, $u_r:X_{r+1}\to X_r$, and $p_d:X_d\to S$ be the ordered affine coordinate tower [def-amb-affine-trace-tower]. For each $r$ use its standard compactification $j_r:X_{r+1}\hookrightarrow P_r=\mathbf P^1_{X_r}$, $q_r:P_r\to X_r$, and set $L_{r,R}=Rq_{r*,R}Dj_{r!,R}$. Let $s_r:T_{P_r}Dj_{r!,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}Dj_{r!,B}T_{X_{r+1}}$ be the open-extension tensor comparison and $b_r:T_{X_r}Rq_{r*,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{r*,B}T_{P_r}$ the proper coefficient map, and put $b^{u_r}=Rq_{r*,B}(s_r)\circ b_rDj_{r!,A}$ [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Define $\mathcal F_{0,R}=1$, $\mathcal F_{r+1,R}=\mathcal F_{r,R}L_{r,R}$, $B_0=1$ and $B_{r+1}=\mathcal F_{r,B}(b^{u_r})\circ B_rL_{r,A}$. Fix any compactification $c=(X_d\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow qS)$ whose middle scheme is in the standing setting, and let $F^c_{d,R}=Rq_{*,R}j_{!,R}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Let $C_{d,R}:\mathcal F_{d,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}F^c_{d,R}$ be the canonical coherent composition and common-refinement comparison on bounded-below inputs [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. Write $\beta_d^c:T_SF^c_{d,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}F^c_{d,B}T_{X_d}$ for the specified proper/open coefficient map [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. For every $M\in\mathcal C_{X_d,A}$,
$$\beta_d^c(M)\circ T_S(C_{d,A,M})=C_{d,B,T_{X_d}M}\circ B_d(M).$$
This holds for the comparison with the specified $c$, including comparison through any common refinement, independently of the auxiliary refinements and parenthesizations. For $d=0$ it uses the identity/composition normalization even when $c$ is a nonidentity compactification of $1_S$. No flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

proof.text: All schemes in the statement are Noetherian: a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applies to every standing finite-type $k$-scheme. The affine tower and its standard line compactifications have the stated separated finite-type maps by [def-amb-affine-trace-tower]. By [lem-sp-etale-ctf-chart-domain], each $L_{r,R}$ and every chosen candidate for $p_r$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$, and coefficient extension also preserves it. Thus all successive inputs, including $L_{r,A}M$, their scalar extensions, and their compact-support images are bounded below. The comparison and coefficient identities used below therefore apply at every stage without assuming that $B$ has finite projective dimension over $A$.

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration: ordered left coefficient square; explicit induction from the canonical binary composition and refinement squares

proof.text: For $u_r$, the specified coefficient arrow of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] is precisely $b^{u_r}=Rq_{r*,B}(s_r)\circ b_rDj_{r!,A}$: that node defines its arrow as the proper coefficient map followed by the open tensor identification. In the identity compactification of $1_S$, the proper counit, open tensor map and identity functors are the identity under their unit identifications; hence $\beta_0=1$. Equivalently this is the identity case of that node's etale-sum normalization, where the sole summand has tensor identification $1$. Consequently the desired equation holds for $r=0$, $C_{0,R}=1$ and $B_0=1$.

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration: ordered left coefficient square; explicit induction from the canonical binary composition and refinement squares

proof.text: For each $1\leq r\leq d$ the separated finite-type map $p_r$ between finite-type $k$-schemes has a compactification $c_r=(X_r\hookrightarrow\overline X_r\to S)$ by [def-asd-compactifiable]; $\overline X_r$ is proper, hence separated of finite type, over $S$, so it is in the standing setting. Choose such auxiliary candidates $H_{r,R}=F^{c_r}_{p_r,R}$, starting with the identity candidate $H_{0,R}=1$. The comparisons of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] give $\alpha_{r,R}:H_{r,R}L_{r,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{r+1,R}$. For the moment fix this parenthesization and define $D_{0,R}=1$ and $D_{r+1,R}=\alpha_{r,R}\circ(D_{r,R}L_{r,R})$. We prove simultaneously for every $M\in\mathcal C_{X_r,A}$ that $\beta_r(M)\circ T_S(D_{r,A,M})=D_{r,B,T_{X_r}M}\circ B_r(M)$, where $\beta_r$ is the specified coefficient arrow for $c_r$. The base is Step 2. This is an induction on $r$ for all inputs, so its hypothesis can be used at $L_{r,A}M$ in the next step.

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration: ordered left coefficient square; explicit induction from the canonical binary composition and refinement squares

proof.text:
Apply the binary composition equality of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] with $f=u_r$, $g=p_r$ and input $M\in\mathcal C_{X_{r+1},A}$. Its input hypotheses hold by Step 1. Writing $T$ with its scheme understood, it says
$$\beta_{r+1}(M)\circ T(\alpha_{r,A,M})=\alpha_{r,B,TM}\circ H_{r,B}(b^{u_r}(M))\circ\beta_r(L_{r,A}M).$$
Precompose this equality with $T(D_{r,A,L_{r,A}M})$ and insert the inductive equality at $L_{r,A}M$. The result is
$$\beta_{r+1}(M)\circ T(D_{r+1,A,M})=\alpha_{r,B,TM}\circ H_{r,B}(b^{u_r}(M))\circ D_{r,B,T L_{r,A}M}\circ B_r(L_{r,A}M).$$

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration: ordered left coefficient square; explicit induction from the canonical binary composition and refinement squares

proof.text:
Naturality of $D_{r,B}:\mathcal F_{r,B}\to H_{r,B}$ at the morphism $b^{u_r}(M):T L_{r,A}M\to L_{r,B}TM$ gives
$$H_{r,B}(b^{u_r}(M))\circ D_{r,B,T L_{r,A}M}=D_{r,B,L_{r,B}TM}\circ\mathcal F_{r,B}(b^{u_r}(M)).$$
Substitute into Step 4 and use the defining recursions for $D_{r+1,B}$ and $B_{r+1}$. Its right side becomes $D_{r+1,B,TM}\circ B_{r+1}(M)$, proving the induction step. This uses only naturality, associativity of composition and functoriality; it introduces no new geometric compatibility.

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration: ordered left coefficient square; explicit induction from the canonical binary composition and refinement squares

proof.text:
Compare the auxiliary final candidate $H_{d,R}$ with the specified $F^c_{d,R}$ by $\phi_R:H_{d,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}F^c_{d,R}$. By [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons], $C_{d,R}=\phi_R\circ D_{d,R}$. The refinement equality of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], also stated there for comparisons through any common refinement, gives $\beta_d^c(M)\circ T(\phi_{A,M})=\phi_{B,TM}\circ\beta_d(M)$. Precomposing with $T(D_{d,A,M})$ and inserting Step 5 yields
$$\beta_d^c(M)\circ T(C_{d,A,M})=\phi_{B,TM}\circ D_{d,B,TM}\circ B_d(M)=C_{d,B,TM}\circ B_d(M).$$
For $d=0$ use $H_{0,R}=1$ and Step 2 in exactly this refinement calculation. Thus an arbitrary compactification of $1_S$ is handled by its normalized comparison with the identity candidate; it is not assumed itself to be the identity compactification.

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration: ordered left coefficient square; explicit induction from the canonical binary composition and refinement squares

proof.text: Finally [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] states that comparison through common refinements is independent of the refinement, satisfies the cocycle condition, and that composition is associative. Its canonical composite $\phi_RD_{d,R}$ is therefore exactly the $C_{d,R}$ in the statement, for every choice of intermediate candidates and parentheses. The coefficient equalities of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] respect those same common-refinement, identity and associativity identifications. Consequently the equation of Step 6 uses the specified maps and is unchanged by any of those auxiliary choices. At $d=1$ its line coefficient arrow is the proper/open composite of Step 2. Every argument used derived coefficient extension on finite-Tor inputs, so no flatness hypothesis has been introduced.

lean.statement: theorem orderedCompactification_scalar_square (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k).Prime] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ ℓ)] {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [Finite A] [CommRing B] [Finite B] (φ : A →+* B) (n : ℕ) (_hA : ((ℓ ^ n : ℕ) : A) = 0) (_hB : ((ℓ ^ n : ℕ) : B) = 0) (S : Scheme.{u}) [S.Over (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (S ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (S ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (S ↘ Spec (.of k))] (d : ℕ) (c : Compactification (affineTraceProjection S d)) (M : _root_.DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf (affineTraceTower S d).smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))) (_hM : etaleProperty A (affineTraceTower S d) M.obj) : ∃ hMB : _root_.DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.plus ((scalarExtension φ (affineTraceTower S d)).obj M.obj), ((scalarExtension φ S).map (orderedCompactificationComparison A k S d c M).hom ≫ etaleCoefficientMap φ c M.obj = orderedAffineCoefficientMap φ S d M.obj ≫ (orderedCompactificationComparison B k S d c ⟨(scalarExtension φ (affineTraceTower S d)).obj M.obj, hMB⟩).hom) ∧ (∀ (c' e : Compactification (affineTraceProjection S d)) (r : e.Refinement c') (s : e.Refinement c), orderedCompactificationComparisonVia A k S d c c' e r s M = orderedCompactificationComparison A k S d c M ∧ orderedCompactificationComparisonVia B k S d c c' e r s ⟨(scalarExtension φ (affineTraceTower S d)).obj M.obj, hMB⟩ = orderedCompactificationComparison B k S d c ⟨(scalarExtension φ (affineTraceTower S d)).obj M.obj, hMB⟩)
lean.note: The ordered functors and coherent composition comparison reuse def-amb-affine-trace-construction. The coefficient map is the literal proper/open recursion; C is the existing bounded-below coherent composition comparison followed by comparison to the specified c, with ambient inclusion identifications. Quantifies over every common refinement and retains arbitrary nonidentity compactifications at d=0. The existential hMB supplies only the bounded-below proof of the actual scalar-extended object, not a substitute object or map. No flatness or finite projective-dimension hypothesis.
